clue.text: Its progress in China is dependant on manpower

definitions.text: Its progress in China is dependant on manpower

blocks.clueFragment: Its progress in China is dependant on manpower
blocks.note: surface reading: an economic remark about China's development relying on its huge workforce
setter's reading: a vehicle that moves along the streets only because a man pulls it

explanation.surface: An observer remarks that China's economic advance relies on its vast labour force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Progress' means literal forward motion, and 'manpower' is the muscle of one man between the shafts.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled passenger cart hauled by a runner, long associated with East Asian cities.

clue.text: Where film is usually not shown

definitions.text: Where film is usually not shown

blocks.clueFragment: Where film is usually not shown
blocks.note: surface reading: a place, such as a theatre, that does not screen movies
setter's reading: unexposed film sits inside a photographic device, and a hearing held privately is closed to the public

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which venues do not screen movies.
explanation.walkthrough: Film is normally kept inside the device that exposes it, never seen until developed; the Latin legal phrase means held in private, away from the public.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal phrase describes proceedings held privately, so a thing done that way is kept from public view.

clue.text: Linked up cables for Jersey, off the Needles?

definitions.text: Linked up cables for Jersey, off the Needles?

blocks.clueFragment: Linked up cables for Jersey, off the Needles?
blocks.note: surface reading: laying undersea telegraph cables to the island of Jersey, past the Needles rocks off the Isle of Wight
setter's reading: a cable is a twisted stitch pattern and a jersey is a sweater, worked off a pair of needles

explanation.surface: Engineers connect telegraph lines to the Channel Island of Jersey, routed past the Needles off the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is a Channel Island and the Needles are chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight, but here a jersey is a pullover and needles are the craft tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a garment by looping yarn into interlinked stitches with two pins, including twisted cable patterns.

clue.text: Old country - hard to leave it when moving

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position, so the letters of leave it change their order

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
the seven letters of the two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hard to emigrate from an old homeland when the time comes to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like the instruction to drop the H, but H stays at the front and 'leave it' is the anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name of Switzerland, from the Roman-era Helvetii tribe, still seen on Swiss stamps and coins.

clue.text: Common expression backing received views?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cliche used to support conventional opinions
setter's reading: the views are picture postcards, and the stock phrase is written on their reverse for the recipient

explanation.surface: A platitude someone trots out in support of orthodox opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Received views' suggests accepted opinions; it means scenic postcards that arrive in the post, and 'backing' means written on their back.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock sentiment holidaymakers scrawl on picture postcards sent home to friends and family.

clue.text: Close friend finally changing sides in the household

indicators.note: the last letter swaps from one side to the other, right becoming left

blocks.note: a familiar is an intimate companion
the closing R (right) gives way to L (left)

explanation.surface: A close friend at last switches allegiance in a domestic quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are the standard abbreviations for right and left, the two sides.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what belongs to or occurs within a family, so things happening among relatives at home.

clue.text: Firm hold on a tree

blocks.note: a cinch is a saddle girth, hence a tight grip
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A climber keeps a secure grip on a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American evergreen genus whose bark yields quinine, used against malaria.

clue.text: Fools entering half of shares to alter tax liability

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the fools are put within the other piece
only one of the two halves of the word shares is kept, the rest dropped

blocks.note: asses are idiots
the second half of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: Idiots buying into stocks prompt the taxman to revise what is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of 'shares' is kept, and the fools go between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate again, as a tax inspector does when revising the sum a taxpayer owes.

clue.text: Look on as perfect fish is served in beer

indicators.note: a drink is served with something placed inside it, so is goes into the beer

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular
taken as written
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A diner regards a fish dish cooked in beer as flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The ide, a European freshwater fish, is a crossword regular worth remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something or someone as flawless, free of the faults it really has.

clue.text: Old soldier's unwell, beset by pains

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded, so the pains enclose the other piece

blocks.note: ill means sick
aches are pains

explanation.surface: An aged veteran, sick and plagued by aches.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'soldier's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Greek warrior of the Trojan War, a fighting man of ancient times.

clue.text: Plant making hot biscuits poorly, short of time

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so the letter for time is dropped
done poorly suggests made badly, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: H for hot, as on a tap
taken as written
T is the symbol for time

explanation.surface: A factory turning out warm biscuits does badly, running behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical shrub of the mallow family with large showy trumpet flowers.

clue.text: Forge common name to cheque's last lines

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word cheque

blocks.note: Smith is the most common British surname
the end letter of the word
RY abbreviates railway, the lines

explanation.surface: A forger adds an everyday name to the final lines of a cheque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forge' looks like the verb to fake, matching the cheque; it is the noun for a blacksmith's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's workshop with hearth and anvil, where metal is heated and hammered.

clue.text: One unaffected by any fare restrictions

definitions.text: One unaffected by any fare restrictions

blocks.clueFragment: One unaffected by any fare restrictions
blocks.note: surface reading: a traveller who does not care about ticket conditions
setter's reading: fare is food, and this creature eats every kind, plant or animal

explanation.surface: A rail passenger shrugs off the small print on cheap tickets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare restrictions' suggests ticket rules, but fare is also what one eats.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal or person that feeds on both plants and meat, with no dietary limits.

clue.text: Composer, poet and playwright

blocks.note: Henry Vaughan, seventeenth-century Welsh metaphysical poet
Tennessee Williams, American dramatist of A Streetcar Named Desire

explanation.surface: A list of three artists from different fields.
explanation.walkthrough: The three nouns read as a list of one person's talents; the second and third surnames combine to make the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Vaughan Williams was the English composer of The Lark Ascending and nine symphonies.

clue.text: See to the French room for concert in South Bank section

blocks.note: V abbreviates vide, Latin for see
French for to the, plural
a concert hall

explanation.surface: A request to arrange a concert room for the French in a South Bank venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The South Bank is the stretch of London south of the Thames; this district in Lambeth also had famous pleasure gardens where concerts were held.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of Lambeth on the south side of the Thames in London, by Vauxhall Bridge.

clue.text: One's possibly found among extreme characters in unsocial terror act

definitions.text: One's possibly found among extreme characters in unsocial terror act

indicators.note: the extreme characters of each word are its outermost letters, first and last
something found among others sits in their midst, so it goes inside

blocks.note: first and last letters of unsocial
first and last letters of terror
first and last letters of act
one is I, and the 's is S

explanation.surface: An extremist might well turn up at the heart of an antisocial act of terrorism.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the person: an extremist is just who might be behind such an act.
explanation.definitionFit: A person holding extreme views, advocating radical measures beyond the ordinary.

clue.text: Maiden heroine upset Shakespeare's queen

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young heroine is distressed by a royal character from the plays.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: The wronged wife of Leontes, king of Sicilia, in The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Unusually, a lighter form of lead monoxide

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters take an abnormal order

blocks.note: the fodder, all eight letters

explanation.surface: A chemistry note says a lighter variety of a lead compound exists.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow or reddish mineral and industrial oxide of lead, used in glass and ceramics.

clue.text: Seed provided by key teachers in group

blocks.note: piano keys are traditionally made of ivory, so ivories are keys
the National Union of Teachers, a body of teachers

explanation.surface: A pupil's seed project comes from the head teachers working together.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was the main British teachers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard seed of a South American palm, carved as a substitute for elephant tusk material.

clue.text: A number turned up in painting as record of former times

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom, so the order flips
in places the flipped piece inside the painting

blocks.note: taken as written
No. is the abbreviation for number
a wall painting

explanation.surface: A numbered detail shows up in a picture that chronicles history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record of former times' reads as a history; it is a gramophone record from before stereo.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-channel sound recording, the norm on discs before stereo arrived in the late 1950s.

clue.text: Beyond rule, riot is breaking out

indicators.note: a riot breaking out is disorder erupting, so these letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A disturbance erupts that defies the rule of law.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lying beyond what is openly stated or evident, as in a hidden motive.

clue.text: Heavenly light

blocks.note: first meaning: of the heavens, celestial
second meaning: delicate and airy, almost weightless

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly light' reads as one phrase about divine radiance, but it is two adjectives with one shared answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both celestial or spiritual and extremely delicate, insubstantial and airy.

clue.text: Flower of youth

blocks.note: surface reading: the bloom of youth, a person's prime
setter's reading: a bloom that sprang from a young man in Greek myth, the beloved of Apollo killed by a discus

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower of youth' is a stock phrase for young people in their prime; here it is a literal flower that grew from a youth's blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The fragrant spring bulb takes its name from Hyacinthus, the mythical boy from whose blood it sprang.

clue.text: King organised test for knightly deeds

blocks.note: ER, Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher of King Edward
ran as in managed or ran a business
a try is a test or attempt

explanation.surface: A monarch sets a trial for his knights to prove their valour.
explanation.definitionFit: The roaming quest for adventure of a medieval knight-errant, as in chivalric romances.

clue.text: Spartan hero's Athenian lover

blocks.note: first meaning: the Spartan admiral who defeated Athens in the Peloponnesian War
second meaning: the young lover of Hermia in A Midsummer Night's Dream, set in Athens

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits a Spartan against his Athenian sweetheart; the two are different men who share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Spartan commander at Aegospotami and to Shakespeare's youth eloping with Hermia.

clue.text: What holds viewer? Ultimate in game and chat shows certainly included

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the very last one of the word game
included means put inside, so the affirmative goes within the rest

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
yes, certainly
to chat is to talk

explanation.surface: A chat show on TV ends a game segment and certainly has viewers hooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' sounds like a TV audience member; it is an eye, and 'chat shows' is not a TV format but chat, then shows as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The movable stalk on which a crab, snail or similar animal carries its eye.
